mainTopic: Purging utensils: the נותן טעם לפגם views on the vessels of מדין, and why gentiles' spits need ליבון while קדשים utensils need only הגעלה
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how each side of the נותן טעם לפגם debate reads the Torah's command to purge the utensils of מדין. The permitting view says the Torah only forbade a קדירה בת יומא, and an older pot is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה. The other view says even a same-day pot gives a spoiled taste, so the Torah itself forbids it. Next, רב עמרם asks רב ששת why our משנה requires ליבון for spits and grills when a teaching about קדשים requires only הגעלה. רב ששת answers that קדשים absorbed something permitted. רבא and אביי each reject that answer or offer their own, and each answer is challenged in turn. רב פפא then explains that an unused utensil gets crusty while one in daily use does not. רב אשי brings back רב ששת's answer, adding that what comes out later is only taste, not the forbidden food itself. Finally the גמרא gives practical details. רבי מני explains how much ליבון is needed and רב הונא explains how הגעלה is done. A story about רב עקביה's large cauldron begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Torah only forbade a pot used that same day
steps.stepSummary: The view that נותן טעם לפגם is permitted explains that the Torah's command to purge the utensils of מדין was only about a קדירה בת יומא. The taste from such a pot is not yet spoiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah forbade only a pot used that same day, because its taste is not a spoiled, harmful taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began just before this text. It explains why, according to the view that permits a spoiled taste, the Torah still required the utensils of מדין to be purged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who holds נותן טעם לפגם מותר must explain why the Torah forbade the vessels of מדין at all. His answer is that the Torah only meant a pot used within the last day. Its absorbed taste is still fresh, so it is not a case of a spoiled taste.

keyTerms.meaning: A pot used for cooking within the last day (literally, 'a pot that is a day old')
Gives a spoiled or harmful taste to the food

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the halachic idea that a pot not used for a full day gives off only a spoiled taste.

phrases.english: [a pot] used that same day,
since it does not give a spoiled taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת יוֹמָאּ, דְּלָאו נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun before this text of how the permitting view reads the command to purge the utensils of מדין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a קדירה בת יומא is forbidden by Torah law, because its taste is not yet spoiled.

steps.title: Then a pot should be allowed after one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this view. If only a same-day pot is forbidden, a pot that has waited past that day should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, it should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view from step 1. If the Torah only forbade a same-day pot, then once a day passes the pot should be fine to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 implies that after one day the taste is spoiled and therefore permitted. Yet the halacha requires purging גיעולי גוים even when they are old. So why not allow an old pot without purging?

keyTerms.meaning: From here on, from that point forward

phrases.english: From then on, let it be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problematic conclusion from the statement in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only a קדירה בת יומא is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the same-day pot is forbidden, an older pot should need no purging, yet the halacha requires purging it.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree forbids the older pot too
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן forbade an older pot so that people would not come to use a same-day pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: a pot not used that same day is forbidden because of a pot used that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. By Torah law the older pot is indeed permitted, but the רבנן forbade it so people would not mix it up with a same-day pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition on an older pot is rabbinic, not from the Torah. It is a protective fence, because a person cannot easily tell whether a non-Jew's pot was used today.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Because of, out of concern for

steps.whatToRemember: Under this view, an older non-Jewish pot is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה. By Torah law, its spoiled taste would be permitted.

phrases.english: It is a decree: a pot not used that same day [is forbidden]
because of a pot used that same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה קְדֵירָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ בַּת יוֹמָאּ מִשּׁוּם קְדֵירָה בַּת יוֹמָאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree. The Torah law stays as stated, but the רבנן add a protective prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An older pot should be fully permitted without purging.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it is permitted, but rabbinically it is forbidden as a fence around the same-day pot.

steps.title: How does the other view read the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the opposing view, which forbids a spoiled taste, understands the command to purge the utensils of מדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other side of the debate. It asks how that view uses the command about the vessels of מדין, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides must account for the same verse. This one-word question opens the explanation for the view that נותן טעם לפגם is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the opposing view)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This refers to the view that a spoiled taste still makes food forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the permitting view to the opposing view on the same verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the view that forbids נותן טעם לפגם reads the command to purge the vessels of מדין.

steps.title: Even a same-day pot gives a spoiled taste
steps.stepSummary: The other view holds that even a same-day pot already spoils the taste. Since the Torah still forbade it, a spoiled taste must be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even a pot used that same day gives a spoiled taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 4. In this view, any absorbed taste in a pot is already spoiled, even on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view disagrees with step 1, which held that a same-day taste is fresh. If even a same-day pot gives a spoiled taste and the Torah still required purging, then the Torah itself forbids נותן טעם לפגם.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views agree that the vessels of מדין needed purging. They argue over whether a same-day pot's taste is fresh or already spoiled, and that decides whether נותן טעם לפגם is permitted.

phrases.english: A pot used that same day also
certainly gives a spoiled taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְדֵירָה בַּת יוֹמָאּ נָמֵי מִפְגָּם פָּגְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a same-day pot spoils the taste, yet the Torah forbade it, which shows that נותן טעם לפגם is forbidden.

steps.title: Heating spits in fire or purging them in hot water?
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם points out a contradiction to רב ששת. Our משנה requires heating spits and grills until white-hot, but a teaching about קדשים says boiling water is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם raised a contradiction to רב ששת. We learned in our משנה that spits and grills must be heated until white-hot in fire. But it was taught about sacrificial meat that the spit and grill are purged in hot water!
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. רב עמרם points out that two sources seem to give different methods for cleaning the same kind of utensils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה, about utensils bought from non-Jews, requires ליבון, heating in fire until white-hot. The teaching about קדשים requires only הגעלה, purging in boiling water, for the very same spit and grill. If hot water works there, why does our משנה demand fire?

keyTerms.meaning: He threw (a contradiction): pointed out two sources that clash
Spit, a metal rod for roasting meat
He heats them in fire until white-hot (ליבון)
He purges them in boiling water (הגעלה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one source is about spits and the other about pots. Both talk about the same utensils, a spit and a grill. That is exactly why the different cleaning methods clash.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב עַמְרָם לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Rav Amram raised a contradiction to Rav Sheshet:
We learned: the spits and the grill —
one heats them until white-hot in the fire,
but it was taught regarding sacrificial meat:
phrases.notes: This teaching appears in זבחים 97a, about roasting utensils used for sacrifices.

phrases.english: the spit and the grill —
one purges them in hot water!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב עַמְרָם לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: which cleaning method roasting utensils require.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in our משנה that spits and grills need ליבון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same utensils are cleaned with only הגעלה when used for קדשים, so why should fire be required for utensils from non-Jews?

steps.title: רב ששת: Sacrifices Absorbed Something Permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that קדשים are different from גיעולי גוים. The spit and grill used for קדשים absorbed permitted food, while the gentile's utensils absorbed forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: עמרם, my son, what do קדשים have to do with the vessels of gentiles? Here the utensil absorbed something permitted. There it absorbed something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רב עמרם's contradiction. He says the two cases are not comparable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, the meat was permitted when the pot absorbed it and only became forbidden later, so boiling water is enough. A gentile's vessel absorbed food that was already forbidden, so it needs the stronger ליבון.

phrases.english: He said to him: Amram, my son,
what does the matter of sacrifices
have to do with purging gentiles' vessels?
Here, it absorbed something permitted;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the spit and grill used for קדשים. The meat was allowed when it was roasted and only became forbidden afterward.

phrases.english: there, it absorbed something forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַמְרָם בְּרִי, מָה עִנְיַן קָדָשִׁים אֵצֶל גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's contradiction from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדשים and gentile vessels should need the same cleaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: A pot that absorbed permitted food needs less than a pot that absorbed forbidden food.

steps.title: רבא: In the End It Releases Something Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב ששת's distinction. When the קדשים pot releases its taste, that taste is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In the end, when it releases the taste, it releases something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the taste the pot gives out now, not what it was when it went in. By now the קדשים taste is forbidden, so the two cases should be treated the same.

phrases.english: Rava said: In the end,
when it releases [the taste],
it releases something forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: סוֹף סוֹף כִּי קָא פָלֵיט אִיסּוּרָא קָא פָלֵיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ששת's whole distinction between permitted and forbidden absorption.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The status of the taste when it comes out is what counts, and that is forbidden in both cases.

steps.title: רבא: The Purging Means Also Rinsing and Scouring
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers his own answer. The 'הגעלה' said about קדשים means rinsing and scouring in addition to ליבון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: What is the purging said there? It means rinsing and scouring as well.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב ששת's answer, רבא gives a new way to resolve the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the קדשים teaching does not mean boiling water alone is enough. It means the vessel also needs the rinsing and scouring the Torah requires for קדשים vessels, on top of ליבון. So there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
What is the "purging" [said there]?
Also rinsing and scouring.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21: the Torah's rule to scour and rinse קדשים vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting step 7, רבא offers a new answer to step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קדשים teaching means boiling water alone is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means rinsing and scouring in addition to ליבון.

steps.title: אביי: Rinsing Is Cold, Purging Is Hot
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that rinsing and scouring cannot be called הגעלה. Rinsing is done with cold water, and הגעלה uses hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are they comparable? Scouring and rinsing are done in cold water, but purging is done in hot water!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הגעלה is a different action from rinsing and scouring. It is unlikely the teaching would use the word for hot purging to mean cold washing, so רבא's reading does not work.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Are they comparable?
Scouring and rinsing are done in cold water,
purging is done in hot water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reading in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that הגעלה means rinsing and scouring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two are different actions, one cold and one hot, so one word cannot mean the other.

steps.title: אביי: Each Source Fills In the Other
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with the principle יגיד עליו רעו. Our משנה mentions ליבון, the other teaching mentions הגעלה, and both are really needed in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: "Its fellow tells about it." Here it taught ליבון, and the same is true for הגעלה. There it taught הגעלה, and the same is true for ליבון.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers his own answer to the contradiction between our משנה and the קדשים teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real disagreement between the two sources. Each one mentions only one requirement and relies on the other source to supply the second, so spits and grills need both ליבון and הגעלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fellow tells about it: one source fills in the other
And the same is true for

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
"Its fellow tells about it":
phrases.notes: איוב 36:33. The idea is that one teaching explains what the other leaves out.

phrases.english: it taught here heating until white-hot,
and the same is true of purging;
it taught there purging,
and the same is true of heating until white-hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: יַגִּיד עָלָיו רֵעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבא's answer, אביי gives a new answer to step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources give different requirements.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both require ליבון and הגעלה, and each mentions only one.

steps.title: רבא: Then One Source Should List Everything
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי. If the principle is יגיד עליו רעו, one source should teach both requirements and the other should teach just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, let it teach all of them in one place, and teach just one in the other place, and then say "Its fellow tells about it"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle יגיד עליו רעו works when one source has the full picture and explains a shorter source. Here each source has only half, so neither one explains the other, and the principle does not fit.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to the contradiction between ליבון and הגעלה have been offered so far: רב ששת (permitted vs. forbidden absorption), רבא (rinsing and scouring), and אביי (יגיד עליו רעו). Each one has been challenged.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If so,
let it teach all of them in one place,
and let it teach one in the other place,
and then say: "Its fellow tells about it"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִי הָכִי, לִתְנִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's use of יגיד עליו רעו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle needs one source with the full list. Here each source has only part of it, so the principle cannot apply.

steps.title: רבא's new reason: each day purges the day before
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops his earlier answer. He explains that קדשים pots need no ליבון because each day's cooking pushes out the previous day's taste before it becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is the reason for קדשים. It follows what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: each and every day becomes the purging for the day before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a brand-new answer for why a קדשים pot does not need ליבון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with any pot is that absorbed taste comes out later after it has become forbidden. With קדשים, the pot is cooked in every day, and each cooking pushes out yesterday's taste while that meat is still allowed to be eaten. So the absorbed taste never gets the chance to become נותר inside the pot, and ליבון is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Purging: pushing absorbed taste out of a utensil
Heating a utensil in fire until it glows

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole approach. The difference between קדשים and non-Jewish utensils is no longer about what kind of taste is absorbed. It is about timing: the taste is removed before it ever becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
With sacrificial meat, this is the reason:

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: It follows what Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh,
who said: Each and every day
becomes the purging for its fellow.
phrases.notes: "Its fellow" means the day before. Today's cooking pushes out yesterday's absorbed taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא challenged אביי in step 12, he gives a new answer to replace his own earlier one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought קדשים pots should need ליבון just like non-Jewish utensils.
steps.terutzMaskana: Daily use purges each day's taste while it is still permitted, so ליבון is unnecessary.

steps.title: This works for peace-offerings but not for sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that daily purging is fine for שלמים, which last two days. A חטאת lasts only a day and a night, so its taste becomes נותר before the next day's cooking pushes it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for שלמים. Since they are eaten over two days, the purging happens before they become נותר. But a חטאת is eaten only for a day and a night. When one cooks a חטאת in the pot today, it becomes נותר. When he cooks in it again tomorrow, whether שלמים or a חטאת, the pot releases the נותר of today's חטאת into tomorrow's חטאת or שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's daily-purging idea by pointing to a חטאת, which has a shorter time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Daily purging only helps if the purge comes before the meat's time runs out. שלמים last two days, so tomorrow's cooking comes in time. A חטאת is already נותר by tomorrow, so tomorrow's cooking would push forbidden taste into the new meat.

keyTerms.meaning: "This works well for...": it fits one case but not another
Peace-offerings, eaten for two days and the night between
Sin-offering, eaten for one day and that night
Leftover sacrificial meat whose time has passed, which is forbidden

phrases.english: This works well for peace-offerings,
since they are eaten over two days,

phrases.aramaic: מִקַּמֵּי דְּנִיהְוֵי נוֹתָר קָא הָוֵי גִּיעוּל.
phrases.english: the purging happens before they become leftover.
But a sin-offering,
since it is eaten for only a day and a night,
when one cooks a sin-offering in it today,
it becomes leftover,
so when he cooks in it again tomorrow,
either a peace-offering or a sin-offering,
it releases the leftover taste of today's sin-offering
into tomorrow's sin-offering or peace-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's new principle from step 13 using the case of a חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle that each day purges the previous day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת becomes נותר before the next day's cooking, so the purge comes too late and forbidden taste enters the new meat.

steps.title: Cook a peace-offering in the same pot on the same day
steps.stepSummary: The answer: after cooking a חטאת in the pot, one cooks שלמים in it that same day. This pushes out the חטאת's taste before it becomes נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: The case we mean is where, after cooking a חטאת in the pot today, he then cooks שלמים in it today as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing how the pot is used: a חטאת and then שלמים on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the חטאת's taste stays in the pot until it becomes נותר. If שלמים are cooked in the pot later that same day, the חטאת's taste is pushed out while it is still permitted. Now the only taste left in the pot belongs to the שלמים, which has a longer time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is needed only for...": introduces the specific case being described

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a חטאת pot needs ליבון after all. The גמרא solves the problem by the order of cooking, not by adding ליבון.

phrases.english: They say: It is needed only for a case
where, when he cooks a sin-offering in it today,
he then cooks a peace-offering in it today as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חטאת challenge from step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חטאת's taste stays in the pot until it becomes נותר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cooking שלמים on the same day pushes out the חטאת's taste in time.

steps.title: How the daily cycle keeps running
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the answer by showing how the cycle repeats. The next day's חטאת and the previous day's שלמים run out together, and then the next day's שלמים purges again.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the next day's חטאת and the previous day's שלמים reach the end of their time together. Then he cooks the next day's שלמים in the pot, and the cycle continues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer by showing that this cooking pattern works day after day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the next day, the pot still holds yesterday's שלמים taste, which is still permitted, so a חטאת can be cooked in it. That day's חטאת and yesterday's שלמים expire at about the same time, and before they do, that day's שלמים are cooked and push both tastes out. This repeats every day, so no taste ever becomes נותר inside the pot.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a קדשים pot needs no ליבון because it is used every day. Each cooking pushes out the earlier taste while it is still permitted. For a חטאת, this works by cooking שלמים in the same pot later that same day.

phrases.english: So the sin-offering of the next day and the peace-offering of the day before
phrases.notes: Picture this from the second day: the חטאת cooked that day, and the שלמים cooked the day before.

phrases.english: reach the end of their time together,
and then he cooks the next day's peace-offering in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the answer from step 15 by showing how the cycle works day after day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining how the case keeps working
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even with same-day שלמים, the next day might still leave forbidden taste in the pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cycle repeats each day, so every taste is pushed out before its time runs out.

steps.title: If daily cooking purges the pot, why is הגעלה needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer. If each day's cooking pushes out the old taste before it becomes forbidden, then even הגעלה should be unnecessary. This challenge to רבא stands, and steps 18 to 20 resolve the original contradiction in other ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, purging with boiling water should not be needed either! This is a real difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's answer proves too much. It would mean the pot needs no koshering at all, yet the משנה requires הגעלה. The גמרא admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explained that no ליבון is needed because the taste never sits in the pot long enough to become נותר. But by that logic, there is never any forbidden taste in the pot, so even boiling water should not be required. The word קשיא means the challenge stands and רבא's answer is set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your explanation is correct
Koshering a utensil by purging it in boiling water
A difficulty; the challenge stands without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word קשיא is a verdict, not a new question. The גמרא is saying this objection to רבא stays unanswered.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, הַגְעָלָה נָמֵי לָא לִיבְעֵי!
phrases.english: If so, purging with boiling water should also not be needed!
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if the pot's taste is always pushed out before it becomes נותר, as רבא said in step 13.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַגְעָלָה נָמֵי לָא לִיבְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the daily-purging answer built up in steps 13 through 16 and ends it as unresolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that daily cooking pushes out the old taste before it becomes forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Proving too much. If the pot never holds forbidden taste, then no koshering at all should be needed, yet the משנה requires הגעלה.

steps.title: A utensil left unused builds up a crust
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. A non-Jew's spit and grill are not used constantly, so they build up a crust and need ליבון. The spit and grill used for קדשים are used every day, so they do not build up a crust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This one gets crusty, and that one does not get crusty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a new answer to the conflict between the two משניות. The difference is about the physical state of the utensil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The non-Jew's spit and grill sit unused between uses, so food residue hardens into a crust, and only fire can remove it. The קדשים spit and grill are used all the time, so no crust forms and boiling water is enough. This answer does not rely on taste being pushed out each day.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets crusty; builds up a hard crust of residue
Koshering a utensil by heating it in fire until it glows

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This one gets crusty, that one does not get crusty.
phrases.notes: The first "this one" is the non-Jew's spit and grill. The second is the spit and grill used for קדשים, which are used every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's answer failed, gives a fresh answer based on the utensil's physical condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the physical state of the utensil (crust versus no crust).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both utensils absorbed forbidden taste, so both should need the same koshering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the unused utensil has a hardened crust that needs fire. The constantly used קדשים pot needs only הגעלה.

steps.title: רב אשי returns to the first answer: permitted versus forbidden when absorbed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי goes back to the original answer. The קדשים pot absorbed a permitted food that only became forbidden later, so הגעלה is enough. The non-Jew's utensil absorbed a forbidden food, so it needs ליבון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, it is as we said at the start. Here it absorbed something permitted, and there it absorbed something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings back the first answer to the conflict, which was challenged earlier. Next he will defend it against that challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the status of the food when the utensil absorbed it. Meat of קדשים was permitted when it went into the pot and only later became נותר. The non-Jew's food was forbidden from the start. A utensil that took in something forbidden needs the stronger koshering.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (used to return to an earlier position)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Really, it is as we said at the start,
phrases.notes: He means the very first answer in this discussion: what counts is whether the food was permitted or forbidden when it was absorbed.

phrases.english: here it absorbed something permitted,
phrases.notes: This is the קדשים pot. The meat was permitted when it was cooked.

phrases.english: here it absorbed something forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer alongside רב פפא's by bringing back the original distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the status of the food at the time it was absorbed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both utensils give out forbidden taste, both should need ליבון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A utensil that absorbed permitted food needs only הגעלה, even if the food became forbidden later. One that absorbed forbidden food needs ליבון.

steps.title: What comes out is only taste, not the forbidden food itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the earlier challenge that the pot gives out forbidden taste. When the pot releases it, the forbidden food itself is not there, only its taste. So we may judge it by the moment it was absorbed, when it was permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what bothers you, that when the pot releases taste it releases something forbidden: when it releases it, the forbidden food is not there in its actual form.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the original answer against the old challenge. He explains why the time of absorbing matters more than the time of releasing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that by the time the קדשים pot releases its taste, that taste is forbidden as נותר. רב אשי answers that what comes out is only taste, not a piece of the forbidden food. Because taste is treated more leniently, its permitted status at the time it was absorbed decides the matter, and הגעלה is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not there in its actual, physical form

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers that still stand for why קדשים pots need only הגעלה. רב פפא: a utensil used daily does not get crusty. רב אשי: the pot absorbed permitted food, and what it releases later is only taste, not the forbidden food itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea about koshering: how a utensil must be koshered can depend on whether the food was permitted or forbidden when it was absorbed.

phrases.english: And as for what bothers you,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's objection back in step 8: in the end, the taste that comes out is forbidden.

phrases.english: that at the time it releases taste
it releases something forbidden,
at the time it releases taste
the forbidden food is not there in its actual form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב אשי's answer by removing the old objection to it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing the objection by separating the forbidden food itself from its released taste.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the taste is forbidden as נותר when it comes out, the pot should count as giving out something forbidden and need ליבון.
steps.terutzMaskana: What comes out is only taste, not the forbidden food itself, so the permitted status at the time it was absorbed decides, and הגעלה is enough.

steps.title: How hot must the utensil get for ליבון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far one must heat utensils for ליבון. רבי מני answers: until their outer layer peels off.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much do we heat them for ליבון? רבי מני says: until their outer layer peels off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the long debate and goes back to a practical detail of the משנה: how much heating counts as ליבון. רבי מני gives the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a spit and grill need ליבון, but it does not say how hot is hot enough. רבי מני gives a visible sign: the utensil is heated until its outer layer flakes off. This gives a clear, practical measure.

phrases.english: And how much does one heat them until white-hot?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the spits and grills from the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said:
Until they shed their outer layer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate about why ליבון or הגעלה is needed and returns to the practical details of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required extent of heating for ליבון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מני: until the utensil's outer layer peels off.

steps.title: How is הגעלה done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to purge utensils with boiling water. רב הונא answers: put a small kettle inside a large kettle of boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we do הגעלה on them? רב הונא says: a small kettle is put inside a large kettle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the next practical question, about how הגעלה is done. רב הונא explains the method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הגעלה, the utensil must be fully in boiling water. A small kettle can simply be dipped into a bigger kettle of boiling water. This method works for small utensils, which leads straight into the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: we purge them with boiling water (הגעלה)

phrases.english: And how does one purge them with boiling water?
Rav Huna said:
A small kettle inside a large kettle.
phrases.notes: He means you dip the small kettle into a bigger kettle full of boiling water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel practical question: after ליבון, now the method of הגעלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: put the small kettle inside a large kettle of boiling water.

steps.title: What about a large kettle?
steps.stepSummary: Since רב הונא's method only works for a small kettle, the גמרא asks how a large kettle is purged.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a large kettle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a gap in רב הונא's answer and asks how to purge a kettle that is too big to fit inside another one. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's method needs a bigger pot to dip the utensil into. A large kettle has no bigger pot to go inside. So the גמרא needs a different method for it.

phrases.english: A large kettle, what does one do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב הונא's method, which only works for a small kettle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to do הגעלה on a kettle too large to put inside another kettle.

steps.title: The incident of רב עקביה's cauldron begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer from a story about a cauldron in the house of רב עקביה that he surrounded with something. The story continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: there was a certain cauldron in the house of רב עקביה, and he surrounded it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the large-kettle question with a real-life incident from רב עקביה's house. The sentence is not finished yet; it continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a rule, the גמרא brings a story of what was actually done with a big cauldron. We are told only that רב עקביה "surrounded it." What he surrounded it with, and how that solved the problem, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא whose house the incident happened in

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of a sentence. Do not try to work out the method yet; what רב עקביה surrounded the cauldron with comes in the next section.

phrases.english: Come and hear: that a certain cauldron
that was in the house of Rav Akavya,
he surrounded it

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּהָהוּא דּוּדָא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי רַב עֲקַבְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about a large kettle with an incident.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not finished yet: רב עקביה surrounded the cauldron with something. The method is completed in the next section.
